population_reconciliation.historical_18720_explanation: The historical manuscript cited '18,720 total sweep trials' (an unexecuted theoretical grid budget). In verified empirical data, results/raw_results.csv contains exactly 13,800 trials (50 seeds, 5 graph families, 21 allocator variants). The primary balanced core grid contains exactly 10,500 trials (750 instances = 50 seeds x 5 families x 3 adversaries; 250 clusters = 50 seeds x 5 families; 14 methods). The remaining 3,300 trials in raw_results.csv are OFAT ablations. The result model corrects this count to the actual data (13,800).
population_reconciliation.seed_vs_cluster_explanation: The README phrase '14 allocators on seeds 1-250' conflated cluster count with seed count. The actual evaluation used seeds 1-50 across 5 graph families, yielding 50 x 5 = 250 independent clusters.
population_reconciliation.heldout_conflict_reduction_explanation: In heldout_v5_results.csv, ACA achieves 39.66 conflicts/trial vs 49.93 for ACA (No Margin), a reduction of 10.27 conflicts (-20.6%). The historical README typo '38.6' is reconciled to the true data value 39.7 (39.66).

bland_altman.interpretation: Physical SITL simulation exhibits a mean bias of -21.78 pp relative to matched discrete graph simulation (95% Limits of Agreement: [-61.00 pp, 17.45 pp]). Differences reflect continuous unicycle kinematics, barrier obstacle interactions, and odometric drift.

collisions_analysis.definition: Rigid-body continuous surface contact events detected in PyBullet simulation (p.getContactPoints > 0) between robot chassis/wheels and static boundary or dynamic blockage barriers.
collisions_analysis.distinction_from_conflicts: Physical collisions measure spatial barrier contacts in continuous physics. Abstract conflicts measure combinatorial double-claims in the decentralized task allocation market.

correlation_with_recourse_detours.interpretation: Physical collision contacts correlate with recourse detours (r = 0.775, p = 0.0000e+00; rho = 0.747, p = 0.0000e+00), confirming that barrier contacts correspond to detected blockage events that trigger contingency branch executions.
